$comment: THE WITNESS DICTIONARY — single machine-readable source of truth for the vocabularies that are duplicated as constants across Rust, Python, JavaScript, and firmware C++. See docs/strategy/13 G1 and Flight Rule FR-13 (docs/FLIGHT_RULES.md). scripts/lint_dictionary_sync.py parses the real source in each language and fails CI if any copy drifts from this file. This is the aviation FRED / ARINC 647A principle: the decode key is a maintained deliverable with the same integrity discipline as the data. To change a vocabulary, edit it here first, then update every copy the linter names.
governance: spec/event_contract.md is the normative prose; this file is its machine-readable projection for the enumerations the linter can check. Where the two disagree, event_contract.md wins and this file is the bug.

event_types.$comment: The kernel's semantic event vocabulary. Source of truth: the Rust `EventType` enum (src/lib.rs), which has no serde rename, so the on-wire string is the PascalCase variant name (the Home Assistant side normalizes CamelCase->snake_case on receipt). `id` is the canonical snake_case identifier used by const.py / the JS card / the adapter `as_str()` form. `label`/`icon` are the canonical Home Assistant presentation, mirrored by const.py EVENT_TYPE_METADATA and www/securacv-timeline-card.js.

failure_types.$comment: System-trace failure records (docs/failure_semantics.md). Rust-only today: the `FailureType` enum (src/lib.rs), PascalCase wire string, no HA mirror. Enumerated here so the dictionary tracks the source and a future mirror can be checked against it. SensorDisagreement and FirmwareIntegrity are defined but not yet emitted (see doc 13 G7).

attestation_tiers.$comment: Provenance of a claim relative to the kernel signature that seals it. Note the modeling asymmetry the linter must respect: the Rust `Attestation` enum (src/lib.rs) has only two variants (adapter, ha-bridged) with explicit serde renames; the device tier is the absent/None case on the Rust wire. The Home Assistant side (const.py, JS card) makes all three explicit strings because it normalizes absent->device on receipt.

claim_kinds.$comment: The vendor-neutral sensor-adapter vocabulary (Track B). Source of truth: the Rust `ClaimKind` enum + `as_str()` + `claim_kind_to_event_type` (src/adapter/contract.rs). Two string forms coexist: the serde PascalCase wire and the snake_case `as_str()` used for dedup keys. The claim->event map is deliberately NOT a string identity (LargeObjectBoundaryCrossing -> boundary_crossing_object_large), so it is stored here as an explicit pair.

modalities.$comment: Sensing medium of a claim, for the timeline glyph. Mirrored const.py MODALITY_METADATA <-> www/securacv-timeline-card.js. `unknown`/`other` are the fallbacks; only the presentation modalities carry {label,icon}.

homekit_projection.$comment: The Apple Home / HAP projection — an EGRESS vocabulary (Track C). Mirrored Rust src/bridge/homekit.rs `HomeSignal` (variants, as_str, hap_characteristic) <-> Swift ios/Sources/SecuraCV/Native/HomeKitBridge.swift `HomeSignal`. Every entry is a coarse present-tense boolean and the list is closed on purpose: there is no zone, timestamp, count, confidence or identity field for a bridge to project, because none exists here to project. `default_enabled: false` marks the class-scoped signals — the one sanctioned step past the dumb-PIR bar (the ObjectClass word, never identity) — which stay off until a human turns them on. `shape` tells the pacer whether a signal is momentary (pulse, auto-clears after the hold window), continuous (level), or sticky (latched, operator-cleared). Design of record: docs/design/apple_home_integration.md. matter_device_type is bridge site D's data-first slice (RFC section 3.5): the same table spoken as Matter sensor device types where one exists, null where Matter has no honest word for the signal (tamper/active/low-battery are HAP status characteristics, and the class-scoped motion signals have no Matter dimension - they ride the parent motion signal). Data only; no Matter stack ships until the HAP lane is stable. `label` is this project's own name for the signal and is mirrored verbatim in the Apple apps (ios/Sources/SecuraCV/Native/HomeKitBridge.swift). `home_app_name` is a DIFFERENT string and not ours to choose freely: it is the per-service Name characteristic the HAP bridge publishes (src/bridge/hap/accessory.rs::service_name), i.e. the words a user actually reads on the tile in Apple's Home app - "Porch Canary - Person", not "Porch Canary - Motion (person)". docs/integrations/apple-home-quickstart.md is generated from this block and told people to look for the label; it now names the tile. The three status signals (tamper/active/low_battery) carry a home_app_name because service_name() defines one for every variant, but they never host a service, so no tile ever bears it. scripts/lint_dictionary_sync.py pins all ten to the Rust.

pacing.$comment: The metronome that keeps this projection inside Invariant III. Publication happens on a fixed cadence, never on an event, so the finest external time resolution anything downstream can learn is one tick — and the publication rate itself carries no information (the 'explicitly configured for cover traffic' path the invariant names). `tick_ms` is a privacy/latency dial, not a performance constant. Bounds are enforced in Rust (PacingConfig::new) and a config outside them is refused, never clamped.

event_signals.$comment: Which signals an event asserts — the egress half of the event vocabulary, mirrored Rust src/bridge/homekit.rs `signals_for_event` <-> Python custom_components/securacv/const.py `HOMEKIT_EVENT_SIGNALS`. Deliberately partial: an event with no honest HAP counterpart maps to [] rather than being forced into a sensor that would misdescribe it, and the two empties are empty for different reasons. AcousticImpulseInZone has no HAP acoustic sensor, and publishing a sound as motion would be a false statement about someone's home. ContactStateChange reports that a contact CHANGED, not what it changed to, while HAP's contact characteristic is a state — deriving one from the other would show a door as open every time it was closed, so the contact signal is driven only by reported state.

signature_format.$comment: The device-signature canonical format (Track A). SCHEMA_V, SIG_PREFIX, ALG_NAME are byte-identical across Python (signature.py) and the firmware copies (firmware/common/identity/device_signature.h and the per-project mirrors). This is the contract doc 12 A3 flags as lacking cross-language golden vectors; PR2 will add those. `canonical_kinds` is the COMPLETE set of Ed25519-signed message kinds in the `securacv-canary-sig|v<schema_v>|<kind>|...` family; scripts/lint_dictionary_sync.py parses the canonical format strings out of the firmware and Python builders and fails on any kind that is implemented but unlisted, or listed but unimplemented. Not every tree carries every kind (canary-display's trust.cpp verifies `chain` only), which is why the gate is union-equals rather than per-file-equals. Two things this comment used to get wrong, both corrected 2026-09-05: `whoami` was missing (firmware/common/identity/device_signature.{h,cpp} `sign_whoami`/`build_whoami_canonical`, pinned by firmware/projects/canary-wap/tests_host/test_device_signature.cpp and rebuilt verifier-side in desktop/src-tauri/src/whoami.rs), and the note that `sense` is absent from the canary-wap tree was false — firmware/projects/canary-wap/arduino/canary_wap/device_signature.{h,cpp} is a byte-identical copy of firmware/common/identity/ and declares sign_sense/build_sense_canonical like every other copy. The kinds a given PRODUCT actually publishes is a different question from the kinds the format defines; this field answers the second. `sentinel` (added 2026-09-23, F22 Phase 1a) is canary-sentinel's fused-claim event: `securacv-canary-sig|v1|sentinel|<device_id>|<seq>|<event>|<level>|<confidence>|<anomaly>|<occupancy>|<range>|<modality_bits>|<bucket_uptime_s>` — every coarse field its chokepoint publishes, so confidence, anomaly and the corroborating-modality bitmask are signed rather than riding beside a `sense` signature that never covered them. Built by firmware/common/identity/device_signature.cpp build_sentinel_canonical (and its byte-identical canary-wap copy), rebuilt by custom_components/securacv/signature.py build_sentinel_event_canonical; both host tests pin the same golden vector.

household_posture.$comment: The household posture: the one thing a household key may change (docs/research/face_id_without_faces.md §6; spec/household_keys_v0.md §2). A posture change is a deliberate, signed act that applies to every event equally; it never rewords, demotes, quiets, collapses or delays a specific witnessed event. It is called the household posture everywhere and never bare `posture`, which already means BODY posture in Vision event JSON (upright / ambiguous / horizontal). `wire` is the posture byte (offset 5) of the signed 112-byte posture statement (magic SCVP, version 1). `unset` has no wire byte because it is never signed: it is what a consumer uses when no statement is available or none passes verification (missing, lapsed, signature not checked against the pinned hub key, another household's, replayed), and it means exactly today's behavior: full sensing, and an attention engine that decides as if household posture did not exist. That is the fail-toward-today rule (research §6.4 rule 6). `set_by` names the credential classes that may set a value (spec §2 principle 4, intent lowers and possession only raises): home, the only value that lowers sensing, needs an intent credential. scripts/lint_dictionary_sync.py pins id, rust_variant and wire to src/relay/attention.rs `HouseholdPosture`, and the signed values' wire bytes to the household crate's `HouseholdPosture::as_byte` (household/src/posture.rs); set_by and the lapse bound in home's effect are recorded here but not yet gated.

values.effect: No valid statement is available. Today's behavior: full sensing everywhere, and the attention engine decides exactly as it does for away. Exists only as a consumer's input; never signed.
Full sensing everywhere. The default and the fail-safe.

Witnesses configured indoor sense tamper only; outdoor, door and unclassified (unknown) witnesses are unchanged, and critical events are critical everywhere. Lapses: not_after is at most 86400 s (HOME_MAX_SECS) after issued_at, default 43200 s.
Full sensing everywhere. Reserved for a future after-hours rule set; in v0 it behaves exactly as away.

attention.$comment: The hub attention engine's vocabulary (spec/household_keys_v0.md §7; docs/design/apple_watch_and_notifications.md §1.1): how loudly the hub tells the household about one event, without identity. Mirrored by src/relay/attention.rs (the pure engine, run by rust.yml's `cargo test --features alert-relay relay::`), pinned by scripts/lint_dictionary_sync.py, and replayed from spec/fixtures/attention_v1.json by every surface that decides tiers. The rules, in the order the engine applies them: (1) a class whose floor is critical is critical whatever the posture, zone, channel, corroboration, novelty, dwell, hour, quiet hours or episode; (2) household posture home on an indoor witness gives none for everything else, the same outcome as the witness sensing tamper only, while outdoor, door and unknown zones are never affected by posture; (3) a class whose ceiling is digest stays digest; (4) an arrival seen on carried radio alone may use the device's own novelty hint, and nothing else may: familiar or unknown stays digest, unfamiliar with sustained dwell may be important, and the phrase and reason are the same whichever hint it was; (5) two or more independent modality classes agreeing, or a camera or radar person, may be important; (6) a single weak channel, or a single strong channel with nothing agreeing, is digest. Quiet hours then hold a digest for the morning summary and never hold important or critical (`held_for_morning`). Household posture unset, away and night give the same decision in v0. Two recorded divergences: quiet hours hold digest only here (spec §7.2, 'Quiet hours hold digests'), while ios/Sources/SecuraCV/Alerts/QuietHours.swift holds everything but critical and the doctrine table's §1.2 says digest and important; and the Apple apps govern repeats per witness, this engine per (episode family, zone). Both are for the Apple apps to reconcile when they replay the vectors. Phrases and reason texts are closed: the only blank any of them has is {zone}, the operator's own name for the zone, filled from the operator's zone table and never from a topic or a payload. None of them says a name, known, unknown, stranger, intruder, recognized, verified, familiar, authorized or household, and the linter refuses one that does (spec §7.2, 'No identity, ever'; Free Signals Invariant F and §5).

tiers.meaning: Not surfaced anywhere. Produced only for a non-critical event from an indoor witness while household posture is home: the hub emulates the witness sensing tamper only.
Pull-only: never pushed, never sounds, visible on the next open and in the morning summary (iOS returns no level at all for it).
Time-sensitive, delivered once. On the LAN only: no important event has a cloud poke class.
Delivered through quiet hours, repeats until acknowledged; the only tier with a cloud poke class.

zone_kinds.meaning: Inside the home. The only kind household posture home acts on.
Outside the home. Never affected by household posture.
At an entry. Never affected by household posture.
The operator has not classified the zone. Treated as never quieted: a zone nobody said is indoor is not indoor.

modalities.$comment: The physical modality classes corroboration counts, after firmware/common/fusion/sentinel_fusion.h `Modality`: evasion is defeated per class, so channels that die together count once (Wi-Fi and BLE on one phone are one carried-radio class; a light sensor and a camera are one optical class). `sentinel_variant` names the sentinel class each one is; acoustic has none because the sentinel has no microphone. max_classes is the cap on a corroboration count and equals the number of classes.

channels.$comment: The reporting channel of an event and the channels that agreed with it. `modality` is the class it counts as (every sentinel channel's class is pinned to firmware/common/fusion/sentinel_fusion.cpp modality_of by the linter; button and microphone are not sentinel channels). `weak` marks a channel that alone is at most digest (spec §7.2 rule 6: radio, sound, motion heat, a light delta; and unknown, so a guess never earns interruption). `sees_person` marks the channels whose person classification may be important on its own (a camera, a radar). Novelty applies only to the carried_radio channels, and only when nothing else agreed. `unknown` has no modality and is never counted.

dwell_bands.$comment: How long the reporting witness says the presence has lasted, banded by the caller. Sustained is at least sustained_secs, the same 90 s as canary-wap notify.h MIN_SUSTAINED_MS (the linter pins both). In v0 only an arrival on carried radio alone reads it.

novelty.$comment: A device's own coarse novelty hint for an arrival seen on carried radio alone (canary-wap familiar.h). An internal input only: it defaults to unknown, its producer waits on the ADR the July 2026 audit requires (item E.16), and it never reaches a phrase, a reason, an event, MQTT or Home Assistant. It cannot make anything critical.

episode_families.$comment: An episode is keyed by (family, zone slot): no device id, no time, no free text. Inside an episode the first decision notifies; a same-or-lower repeat collapses into it and notifies again only after its earned rest (episode_governor); a higher tier always notifies, and critical is never governed (spec §7.2, 'One episode, one notification'). `cloud_class` is the relay poke class (src/relay/mod.rs `PokeClass` wire word) a critical decision of that family maps to; every other family has none, so household posture and activity never create a remote poke class.

episode_governor.$comment: Repeat governance, ported from the Apple apps' RepeatGovernor (ios/Sources/SecuraCV/Alerts/RepeatGovernor.swift; the linter pins its three constants too) so hub and phone rest a burst the same way: the first of an episode notifies; a same-or-lower repeat notifies again only after its earned rest (base_cooldown_secs doubling per notification to cooldown_cap_secs); calm_gap_secs with no repeat even considered ends the episode; a higher tier always notifies; critical is never governed; none is never considered. Seconds are the caller's monotonic clock.

phrase_ids.$comment: Phrases and reason texts are closed: the only blank any of them has is {zone}, the operator's own name for the zone, filled from the operator's zone table and never from a topic or a payload. None of them says a name, known, unknown, stranger, intruder, recognized, verified, familiar, authorized or household, and the linter refuses one that does (spec §7.2, 'No identity, ever'; Free Signals Invariant F and §5).

items.text: The witness log failed its integrity check

reason_codes.$comment: Why a decision came out as it did: the 'why did or didn't I get this' trace (doctrine §1.2), one closed code per rule. The reason names the rule, never an input the rule must not reveal: an arrival on carried radio alone has the same reason whatever its novelty hint was. Phrases and reason texts are closed: the only blank any of them has is {zone}, the operator's own name for the zone, filled from the operator's zone table and never from a topic or a payload. None of them says a name, known, unknown, stranger, intruder, recognized, verified, familiar, authorized or household, and the linter refuses one that does (spec §7.2, 'No identity, ever'; Free Signals Invariant F and §5).

items.text: Tamper, a log failure, a dark witness and a heard smoke or CO alarm are always critical.
Home posture: indoor witnesses report tamper only.
Home posture: this witness was sensing tamper only.
This kind of event never interrupts on its own.
An event this hub has no word for is never more than a digest.
Two or more independent kinds of sensing agreed.
A camera or a radar saw a person.
One weak channel alone (radio, sound, motion heat or light) is never more than a digest.
Nothing independent agreed, so it waits in the digest.

classes.$comment: The coarse event classes. `floor_tier` is the tier a class gets when nothing earns it more; a critical floor is never lowered, and the only thing that takes a non-critical class below digest is household posture home on an indoor witness. `ceiling_tier` is the most a class can earn (corroboration, a camera or radar person, an unfamiliar sustained radio arrival). `person_class` marks the classes a camera or radar person classification may make important on its own. `family` keys the episode; `phrase` is the class's one closed phrase, so neither household posture nor novelty can change the wording.

class_map.$comment: Every event word the hub can see, in both dialects, mapped to one class. `kernel_event_types` is keyed by exactly the event_types ids above (the kernel's sealed vocabulary; src/relay/attention.rs matches the Rust EventType exhaustively, so a new kernel variant does not compile until it is mapped). `device_words` are the Canary wire words (the `event` of securacv/<id>/events, the acoustic chokepoint's type_name, the integrity words) that this dictionary deliberately does not govern as event types (ios/Shared/EventVocabulary.swift `DeviceEvent` says why). Matching is exact and case-sensitive. Any word not listed is `unknown_word_class`, whose ceiling is digest: an unknown word falls back to digest and is never critical; like every non-critical class it is none only under rule 2 (household posture home on an indoor witness, which the engine applies before rule 3). A message on securacv/<id>/tamper is tamper by its topic, whatever its kind or type word (as the relay's evaluate() already treats it), so those words are not listed. THE SEVERITY SETTLEMENT (2026-10-13). Three surfaces mapped events to severity and disagreed: the Apple apps (EventVocabulary.swift defaultSeverity, then AlertCenter.level(for:), where only the tamper rung is critical, only alert is important and everything lower is pull-only), the display (firmware/projects/canary-display/src/fleet/fleet_model.cpp classify_event, substring matches) and the relay (src/relay/mod.rs, four poke classes and no activity at all). This table settles them; a surface that disagrees with it is the bug. (1) chain_break, verify_failed, witness_lost: iOS alert (important); settled critical, beside tamper and the two heard life-safety cadences, as the doctrine table (apple_watch_and_notifications.md §1.1) already says: tamper, chain-integrity failure, a witness declared dark. (2) smoke_alarm_t3, co_alarm_t4: iOS alert (important), display Alert (sounds through quiet hours), relay pattern at ntfy priority 5; settled critical, because a smoke alarm that honors quiet hours is a decoration (QuietHours.swift). Each keeps its own class and phrase: smoke and CO ask for different responses. (3) glass_break: iOS warn (pull-only), display Alert; settled digest alone, important when an independent class agrees, never critical. It is one microphone's cadence classification and a dropped glass makes the same sound (rule: a single weak channel is at most digest), and critical is reserved for what may pierce quiet hours. The display's Alert is the outlier. (4) doorbell, knock and the boundary, restricted-zone, after-hours and removed-object kernel events: iOS notice (pull-only), display Warn; settled digest alone and important when corroborated. A Vision doorbell press is two classes (its button and its camera) and is important; a doorbell heard by a microphone alone is digest. (5) person and presence words: iOS notice (never pushed today); settled by the corroboration rule, so a camera or radar person, or any two independent classes, may be important. That is new behavior on the LAN only: no important event has a cloud poke class, and the relay's vocabulary is unchanged (src/relay/mod.rs: widening it is a privacy decision). (6) panic stays tamper; iOS and the display already agree. (7) An unknown word: iOS and the display both fall to their calm floor; settled other, ceiling digest.

known_divergences.$comment: Vocabularies that are NOT unified today and are deliberately NOT gated by the linter yet, because unifying them needs a design decision, not a rename. Recorded here so they are captured, not lost. Each maps to a discrepancy id from the inventory and a follow-up. One exception lives here because it sits beside the divergence it partly closes: tamper_vocabularies.system_integrity_kinds IS unified and IS gated (scripts/lint_dictionary_sync.py).

tamper_vocabularies.note: Two 'tamper' vocabularies share securacv/<id>/tamper. (1) GATED: system_integrity_kinds below, the kinds the system.integrity csi_event module (firmware/common/csi/src/tamper_events_module, registered by canary-wap and by the canary PIO tree) can emit. They are the HA integration's tamper *types* verbatim (custom_components/securacv/const.py TAMPER_*): canary-wap's csi_mqtt bridges every system.integrity commit onto the tamper topic as {"type":"<kind>"}, which is exactly what HA's per-type binary sensors match (the canary PIO tree's csi_event_egress bridges its SD and enclosure kinds the same way; its boot story reaches that topic through the power-events classifier). scripts/lint_dictionary_sync.py requires the module's kind literals and its header's doctrine table to equal this list, each kind to be a const.py TAMPER_* value with its own per-type sensor and not in FUTURE_TAMPER_TYPES, and every narration copy (the HA timeline card, HA voice alerts, the canary-wap dashboard, the Apple apps' TamperKind) to know it. (2) firmware_kinds, the older semantic device-tamper `kind` (enclosure_tamper | temp_drift | camera_tamper) the canary PIO tree's sensing-witness drain publishes; these fold to EventType::TamperDetected upstream and are otherwise NOT unified with HA's types (inventory D4/D5/D6; unifying them is a product decision tracked separately, relates to doc 11 device-model consolidation). The one exception is firmware_kind_types: a kind that IS one of HA's tamper types also carries that word as `type` on the same payload (the touch pad's enclosure_tamper is HA's `enclosure`), gated like (1) on the HA side and required by the linter in the canary drain's code.

system_integrity_hosts.$comment: Which kinds each host's feeds can produce. Boot kinds come from the reset reason every board has; sd_error / sd_remove need a live SD state (canary-wap: hardware_state.h SdState; canary: the storage lane via common/storage/sd_mount_policy.h sd_state_for_tamper, FEATURE_SD_STORAGE builds); enclosure needs a debounced contact state (common/csi/src/contact_tamper.h over the board map's TAMPER_PIN_DEFAULT), compiled only with FEATURE_TAMPER_GPIO=1, which no shipped profile sets until the pin is bench-validated. The linter requires every host list to be a subset of system_integrity_kinds, their union to equal it, and each host that lists an SD kind or enclosure to still pass the matching live feed.

mqtt_topic_namespaces.note: Three disjoint topic namespaces reflect the three-entity-universe finding (doc 11 section 1.1): the Rust PWK->HA bridge publishes under `witness/...` (zone tree + chain_problem/last_event/digest); firmware canaries and the HA integration use `securacv/<id>/...` (flat suffixes). These are not mirrors and must not be gated as if they were. Consolidation is doc 11 issue #930. Inventory D8/D9.
